rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one soul is Adam; this origin is a favor because common descent should bring people closer to mutual affection.
rows.anchor: يعني آدم , وفي ذلك نعمة عليكم لأنه أقرب إلى التعاطف بينكم .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Hasan say Eve was created from Adam's rib.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس , ومجاهد , والحسن خلقت من ضلع آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view specifies the left rib, which explains the saying that woman is a crooked rib.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأيسر , ولذلك قيل للمرأة : ضلع أعوج .

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet at the verse's revelation says woman was created from man, whose concern is woman, while man's concern is clay.
rows.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال عند نزولها عليه :

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibrahim understand asking through God and kinship as the formula “I ask you by God and by kin”; Hamza reads al-arham in the genitive on this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد وإبراهيم , وقرأ حمزة والأرحام بالكسر على هذا المعنى .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi instead read the phrase as a command to maintain kinship and not sever it; the opening's common origin means people are siblings, even when distant.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد صلوها ولا تقطعوها , وهو قول قتادة , والسدي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains raqib as a guardian or preserver.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : حفيظا , وهو قول مجاهد .

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd explains raqib as knowing or all-aware.
rows.anchor: والثاني : عليما , وهو قول ابن زيد .

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, Abu Qilaba, al-Zuhri, Makhul, and Ibn Zayd take the married women as forbidden except those captured in war.
rows.anchor: يعني ذوات الأزواج إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم بالسبي , وهذا قول علي

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that after the Prophet captured the people of Awtas, the Companions asked how they could have relations with captive women whose lineages and marriages they knew; this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : لما سبى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أهل أوطاس , قلنا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Jabir, Anas, Ibn Abbas in Ikrima's narration, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Hasan say married women are forbidden to others, but buying an enslaved woman ends her marriage and makes her lawful to the buyer.
rows.anchor: حرام على غير أزواجهن إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم من الإماء , إذا اشتراها مشتر بطل نكاحها وحلت لمشتريها ويكون بيعها طلاقها , وهذا قول ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan lists sale, emancipation, gift, inheritance, or the husband's divorce among the events that dissolve an enslaved woman's marriage.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : طلاق الأمة يثبت نسبها , وبيعها , وعتقها , وهبتها , وميراثها , وطلاق زوجها .

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Aliya, Ubayda al-Salmani, Ata, and al-Suddi interpret the married women as chaste women, except those lawful through marriage contract or ownership.
rows.anchor: أن المحصنات من النساء العفائف إلا ما ملكت أيمانكم بعقد النكاح , أو ملك اليمين , وهذا قول عمر

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id says the verse concerned women who emigrated to the Prophet while married; Muslims married them, then their husbands emigrated, and Muslims were prohibited from marrying them.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي سعيد الخدري .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of iḥsan is prevention; a fortress prevents an enemy, armor is protective, a horse protects its rider, and a chaste woman restrains herself from indecency.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإحصان المنع , ومنه حصن البلد , لأنه يمنع من العدو , ودرع حصينة أي منيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chaste-woman sense is also used of Mary, who guarded her chastity.
rows.anchor: ومنه ^ { ومريم ابنة عمران التي أحصنت فرجها } ^ [ التحريم : 12 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God's book upon you” can mean God has prescribed this prohibition in writing.
rows.anchor: أن معناه : حرم ذلك عليكم كتابا من الله .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God's book upon you” can mean that people must adhere to God's book.
rows.anchor: معناه ألزموا كتاب الله .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading makes God's book the overseer of what people deem lawful or forbidden.
rows.anchor: أن كتاب الله قيم عليكم فيما تستحلونه وتحرمونه .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi takes “beyond that” to mean fewer than five women.
rows.anchor: أن معناه ما دون الخمس , وهو قول السدي .

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata takes “beyond that” to mean relatives outside the prohibited degrees of kinship.
rows.anchor: ما وراء ذوات المحارم من أقاربكم , وهو قول عطاء .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes “beyond that” to mean other women among those owned by one's right hand.
rows.anchor: ما وراء ذلكم مما ملكت أيمانكم , وهو قول قتادة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking women with one's wealth means paying either a purchase price or a marriage dower.
rows.anchor: يعني أن تلتمسوا بأموالكم إما شراء بثمن , أو نكاحا بصداق .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Chaste, not fornicating” means marrying rather than committing fornication; sifah literally evokes pouring fluid, as with tears or water running down a mountain, and names illicit ejaculation.
rows.anchor: يعني متناكحين غير زانين , وأصل السفاح صب الماء , ومنه سفح الدمع إذا صبه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan, and one view of Ibn Abbas understand the command to give the women their known dowers.
rows.anchor: أي آتوهن صدقاتهن معلومة , وهذا قول مجاهد , والحسن , وأحد قولي ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second view treats the passage as temporary marriage for a fixed term without a marriage contract; Ibn Abbas read “for a fixed term,” as did Ubayy, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and al-Suddi.
rows.anchor: أنها المتعة إلى أجل مسمى من غير نكاح , قال ابن عباس كان في قراءة أبي

rows.speaker: الحكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakam attributes to Ali the statement that, had Umar not prohibited temporary marriage, only a wretched person would fornicate.
rows.anchor: وقال الحكم : قال علي : لولا أن عمر نهى عن المتعة ما زنى إلا شقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi says the report attributed to Ali is not established and notes that the account from Ibn Abbas is contrary, saying Ibn Abbas later repented of temporary marriage.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يثبت , والمحكي عن ابن عباس خلافه , وأنه تاب من المتعة

rows.speaker: سليمان بن المعتمر
rows.claim: Sulayman ibn al-Mu'tamir says spouses who agreed on a dower may mutually reduce it if the husband later becomes unable to pay.
rows.anchor: لا حرج عليكم أيها الأزواج إن أعسرتم بعد أن فرضتم لنسائكم مهرا عن تراض أن ينقصنكم منه ويتركنكم , وهذا قول سليمان بن المعتمر .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says partners in temporary marriage may mutually extend the term and increase payment after it expires, before the woman observes the waiting period to establish an unpregnant womb.
rows.anchor: لا جناح عليكم أيها الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the clause as allowing mutually agreed payment to be returned to the men.
rows.anchor: لا جناح عليكم فيما تراضيتم به ودفعتموه أن يعود إليكم عن تراض , وهذا قول ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God knew all things before creating them and is wise in their determination and management.
rows.anchor: كان عليما بالأشياء قبل خلقها , حكيما في تقديره وتدبيره لها , وهذا قول الحسن .

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says people witnessed knowledge and wisdom and were told that God has always been so.
rows.anchor: أن القوم شاهدوا علما وحكمة فقيل لهم إن كان كذلك لم يزل , وهذا قول سيبويه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufan grammarians explain the past-tense report as standing in place of a future-tense report.
rows.anchor: أن الخبر عن الماضي يقوم مقام الخبر عن المستقبل وهذا مذهب الكوفيين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ṣiddīqūn are followers of the prophets; the word ṣiddīq may derive from truthfulness or from charity.
rows.anchor: أما الصديقون فهو جمع صديق , وهم أتباع الأنبياء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed derivation of ṣiddīq is the word for truthfulness.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه فعيل من الصدق .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other proposed derivation of ṣiddīq is the word for charity.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أنه فعيل من الصدقة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuhadāʾ are those killed in God's path.
rows.anchor: وأما الشهداء فجمع شهيد , وهو المقتول في سبيل الله تعالى .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of “martyr” is that the person bears witness to the truth until being killed in God's path.
rows.anchor: لقيامه بشهادة الحق , حتى قتل في سبيل الله .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the martyr witnesses God's honor in the afterlife and testifies about people's deeds on Judgment Day, if killed in God's path at life's end.
rows.anchor: لأنه يشهد كرامة الله تعالى . في الآخرة . ويشهد على العباد بأعمالهم يوم القيامة إذا ختم له بالقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥūn may mean everyone whose deeds are sound, or everyone whose inward and outward state is sound.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه كل من صلح عمله . والثاني : هو كل من صلحت سريرته وعلانيته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafīq may derive from gentleness in action or gentleness while traveling.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه مأخوذ من الرفق في العمل . والثاني : أنه مأخوذ من الرفق في السير .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada, al-Rabi', and al-Suddi say people feared they would not see the prophets in Paradise, since the prophets would be in the highest ranks; they grieved and asked the Prophet, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن ناسا توهموا أنهم لا يرون الأنبياء في الجنة لأنهم في أعلى عليين , وحزنوا وسألوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “proof” from God is the Prophet, whose miracle testifies to his truthfulness.
rows.anchor: هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , لما معه من المعجز الذي يشهد بصدقه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear light is the Quran, called light because it makes truth visible as light makes visible things perceptible.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن سمي نورا لأنه يظهر به الحق , كما تظهر المرئيات بالنور .

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says those who hold fast hold fast to the Quran.
rows.anchor: اعتصموا بالقرآن , وهذا قول ابن جريج .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they seek God's protection from Satan's deviation and human desire.
rows.anchor: اعتصموا بالله من زيغ الشيطان وهوى الإنسان .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says guidance to the straight path is giving believers in this world what leads them to the bliss of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أن يعطيهم في الدنيا ما يؤديهم إلى نعيم الآخرة , وهذا قول الحسن .

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين البصريين
rows.claim: Some Basran exegetes say the guidance is leading believers in the afterlife along the road to Paradise.
rows.anchor: هو الأخذ بهم في الآخرة إلى طريق الجنة , وهو قول بعض المفسرين البصريين .

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib says the last complete sura revealed was al-Bara'a, while the last verse revealed was the ending of Surat al-Nisa, “they ask you.”
rows.anchor: قال البراء ابن عازب : آخر سورة نزلت كاملة سورة براءة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir says this verse was revealed about him: while ill, he asked the visiting Prophet what to do with his wealth because he had nine sisters; the Prophet gave no answer until it was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقال جابر بن عبد الله : نزلت هذه الآية في

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin says the verse came while the Prophet traveled with Hudhayfa at his side; the Prophet told it to Hudhayfa, who conveyed it to Umar following behind.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين : نزلت هذه الآية على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو في مسيرة

none: A bare sura heading and basmala only.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the covenants are God's commitments of faith taken from His servants about what He permits and forbids.
rows.anchor: أنها عهود الله , التي أخذ بها الإيمان , على عباده فيما أحله لهم , وحرمه عليهم , وهذا قول ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says these are God's covenants with the People of the Book to follow the Torah and Gospel in affirming Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أنها العهود التي أخذها الله تعالى على أهل الكتاب أن يعملوا بما في التوراة , والإنجيل من تصديق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes the covenants to be pre-Islamic alliances.
rows.anchor: أنها عهود الجاهلية وهي الحلف الذي كان بينهم , وهذا قول قتادة .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan takes the covenants to cover all the obligations of religion.
rows.anchor: عهود الدين كلها , وهذا قول الحسن .

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes them as people's contracts of sale or marriage and personal commitments such as vows or oaths.
rows.anchor: العقود التى يتعاقدها الناس بينهم من بيع , أو نكاح , أو يعقدها المرء على نفسه من نذر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Suddi take livestock animals to mean all camels, cattle, and sheep.
rows.anchor: أنها الأنعام كلها , وهي الإبل , والبقر , الغنم , وهذا قول قتادة , والسدي .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar include livestock embryos found dead in their mothers after the mothers are slaughtered.
rows.anchor: أنها أجنة الأنعام التى توجد ميتة فى بطون أمهاتها , إذا نحرت أو ذبحت , وهذا قول ابن عباس , وابن عمر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view includes wild gazelles and cattle but excludes hoofed animals, since the term is derived from the comfort of walking.
rows.anchor: أن بهيمة الأنعام وحشيها كالظباء وبقر الوحش , ولا يدخل فيها الحافر , لأنه مأخوذ من نعمة الوطء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word sha'a'ir means God's signs or markers and derives from informing or making known.
rows.anchor: أى معالم الله , مأخوذ من الإشعار وهو الإعلام .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid interpret God's signs as the rites of pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: أنها مناسك الحج , وهو قول ابن عباس , ومجاهد .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas interprets God's signs as what God has forbidden while in consecration.
rows.anchor: أنها ما حرمه الله فى حال الإحرام , وهو مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the signs as God's sanctuaries.
rows.anchor: أنها حرم الله , وهو قول السدي .

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata interprets the signs as God's limits governing what He permits, forbids, allows, and bars.
rows.anchor: أنها حدود الله فيما أحل وحرم وأباح وحظر , وهو قول عطاء .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets the signs as the whole religion of God, linking the phrase about honoring God's signs to honoring God's religion.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : ^ { ذلك ومن يعظم شعآئر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacred month must not be treated as permitting fighting.
rows.anchor: أي لا تستحلوا القتال فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the sacred month as Rajab of Mudar.
rows.anchor: أنه رجب مضر .

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima identifies the month as Dhu al-Qi'da.
rows.anchor: أنه ذو العقدة , وهو قول عكرمة .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the sacred month as the sacred months collectively.
rows.anchor: أنها الأشهر الحرم , وهو قول قتادة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of the offering is anything a person dedicates to the House of God.
rows.anchor: أنه كل ما أهداه من شيء إلى بيت الله تعالى .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says an offering can be uncollared livestock that someone has vowed to dedicate and collar.
rows.anchor: أنه ما لم يقلد من النعم , وقد جعل على نفسه , أن يهديه ويقلده , وهو قول ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the garlands as collars on sacrificial animals and considered a person consecrated once he collared an offering.
rows.anchor: أنها قلائد الهدي , وهو قول ابن عباس , وكان يرى أنه إذا قلد هديه صار محرما .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says polytheists wore collars made from tree bark while traveling to and from Mecca to secure safety.
rows.anchor: قلدوها فى ذهابهم إلى مكة , وعودهم ليأمنوا , وهذا قول قتادة .

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says departing polytheists wore bark taken from the sanctuary for safety, so they were forbidden to strip sanctuary trees for collars.
rows.anchor: أن المشركين كانوا يأخذون لحاء الشجر من الحرم إذا أرادوا الخروج منه , فيتقلدونه ليأمنوا , فنهوا أن ينزعوا شجر الحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those going to the Sacred House are people intending to reach it; the verb amama means to aim for a place, also expressed as yammama.
rows.anchor: يعنى ولا تحلوا قاصدين البيت الحرام , يقال أممت كذا إذا قصدته , وبعضهم يقول يممته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited anonymous verse uses yammamtu, “I aimed,” as evidence for the verb meaning to head for a place.
rows.anchor: يقال أممت كذا إذا قصدته , وبعضهم يقول يممته , كقول الشاعر :

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar understands seeking God's bounty as earning profit through trade.
rows.anchor: الربح فى التجارة , وهو قول ابن عمر .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid understands bounty as reward, and God's pleasure as His approval of the pilgrims' rites.
rows.anchor: الأجر , وهو قول مجاهد { ورضوانا } يعني رضي الله عنهم بنسكهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to hunt after leaving consecration follows a prohibition, so it grants permission rather than making hunting obligatory.
rows.anchor: وهذا وإن خرج مخرج الأمر , فهو بعد حظر , فاقتضى إباحة الاصطياد بعد الإحلال دون الوجوب .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kisa'i, and Abu al-Abbas al-Mubarrad read yajrimanakum as “let it not carry you”; the phrase can mean that someone drove me to hate you.
rows.anchor: لا يحملنكم , وهو قول ابن عباس , والكسائي , وأبي العباس المبرد يقال : جرمني فلان على بغضك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra' reads the verb as “let it not earn you” or “cause you to acquire”; he cites the expression for earning for one's family.
rows.anchor: معناه ولا يكسبنكم , يقال جرمت على أهلي , أي كسبت لهم , وهذا قول الفراء .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas understands shana'an as hatred.
rows.anchor: معناه بغض قوم , وهذا قول ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands shana'an as enmity.
rows.anchor: عداوة قوم , وهو قول قتادة .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse concerned al-Hutam ibn Hind al-Bakri: after questioning the Prophet about his message, leaving treacherously, and stealing Medina livestock, he returned the next year as a pilgrim with garlanded offerings; when Companions sought permission to kill him, the Prophet refused because he had collared an offering.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية فى الحطم بن هند البكري أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم , إلام تدعو ؟

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the whole verse was abrogated; al-Mawardi notes agreement that some part of it was abrogated.
rows.anchor: ان جميعها منسوخ , وهذا قول الشعبي , قال : لم ينسخ من المائدة إلا هذه الآية .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say the abrogated portions are “nor the sacred month” and “nor those going to the Sacred House.”
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس , وقتادة .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the abrogated part was the pre-Islamic practice of wearing collars made from tree bark.
rows.anchor: الذي نسخ منها ما كانت الجاهلية تتقلده من لحاء الشجر , وهذا قول مجاهد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-tayyibat means lawful things; lawful things are called good even when not pleasurable, by analogy with what people enjoy.
rows.anchor: يعني بالطيبات الحلال , وإنما سمي الحلال طيبا , وإن لم يكن مستلذا تشبيها بما يستلذ .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jawarih are hunting animals, beasts or birds, that earn prey for their owners; the word derives from earning, as in the cited line by al-A'sha of Banu Tha'laba, where ajtaraḥ means “acquired.”
rows.anchor: سميت جوارح لكسب أهلها بها من قولهم : فلان جارحة أهله أي كاسبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-A'sha of Banu Tha'laba's cited word ajtaraḥ is evidence for the sense “acquired.”
rows.anchor: ذا جبار منضجا ميسمه … يذكر الجارح ما كان اجترح … أي ما اكتسب

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi restrict mukallibin to dogs, making only dog-caught game lawful.
rows.anchor: يعني من الكلاب دون غيرها , وأنه لا يحل إلا صيد الكلاب وحدها , وهذا قول ابن عمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ali ibn al-Husayn, al-Hasan, and Mujahid say taklib describes trained hunting predators, including non-dogs, made eager for the hunt like dogs.
rows.anchor: أن التكليب من صفات الجوارح من كلب وغيره , ومعناه مضرين على الصيد كما تضري الكلاب , وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view treats taklib as an attribute of the predator meaning that it has been trained.
rows.anchor: أن معنى التكليب من صفات الجارح : التعليم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Training means teaching predators to seek game for people through the discipline and training methods God has taught.
rows.anchor: أى تعلمونهن من طلب الصيد لكم مما علمكم الله من التأديب الذي أدبكم وصفات التعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trained predator is released when sent, responds when called, and holds its prey when it catches it.
rows.anchor: فهو أن يشلى إذا أشلي , ويجيب إذا دعي ويمسك إذا أخذ .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ata say refraining from eating the catch is required for every hunting animal; if it eats, the catch is not lawful.
rows.anchor: أنه شرط في كل الجوارح , فإن أكلت لم تؤكل , وهذا قول ابن عباس , وعطاء .

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Hurayra, and Salman say refraining from eating is not required for any hunting animal, and its catch remains lawful if eaten.
rows.anchor: أنه ليس بشرط فى كل الجوارح ويؤكل وإن أكلت , وهذا قول ابن عمر

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, and al-Suddi require non-eating for mammalian predators but not birds, so a bird's catch is lawful even if the bird eats.
rows.anchor: أنه شرط في جوارح البهائم فلا يؤكل ما أكلت , وليس بشرط في جوارح الطير , فيؤكل وإن أكلت

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi' reports that Gabriel refused to enter a house with a dog; after the Prophet ordered dogs killed, a woman kept one barking by her, and Abu Rafi' killed it on the Prophet's renewed order. People then asked what was lawful to them from the kind of animal they had been ordered to kill, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رافع قال : جاء جبريل

rows.speaker: زيد الخير
rows.claim: A second account says Zayd al-Khayl, renamed Zayd al-Khayr by the Prophet, asked about Dureih and Abu Dujana, whose five dogs hunted gazelles; the verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: ما حكي أن زيد الخيل لما وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال فيه من الخير ما قال فسماه زيد الخير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as related by Hisham, names the five dogs al-Mukhtalis, Ghallab, al-Ghanim, Sahlib, and al-Muta'ati.
rows.anchor: وحكى هشام عن ابن عباس أن أسماء هذه الكلاب الخمسة التي لدريح وأبي دجانة : المختلس وغلاب والغنيم وسهلب والمتعاطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb la-yabluwannakum may mean God will impose obligations on you.
rows.anchor: في قوله ليبلونكم تأويلان : أحدهما : معناه ليكلفنكم .

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub and al-Kalbi take la-yabluwannakum to mean God will test you.
rows.anchor: ليختبرنكم , قاله قطرب , والكلبي . وفي قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes min in min al-sayd as partitive: the rule covers land rather than sea game, and game in the sanctuary or during consecration rather than outside them.
rows.anchor: أن { من } للتبعيض في هذا الموضع لأن الحكم متعلق بصيد البر دون البحر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes min as marking the kind, as in the command to avoid impurity from idols.
rows.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى : ^ { اجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان } ^ [ الحج : 30 ] قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says hands reach eggs and spears reach game.
rows.anchor: ما تناله أيدينا : البيض , ورماحنا : الصيد , قال مجاهد .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says hands reach small game and spears reach large game.
rows.anchor: ما تناله أيدينا : الصغار , ورماحنا : الكبار , قاله ابن عباس .

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi takes “that God know” to mean “that God see,” using knowledge for sight because sight leads to knowledge.
rows.anchor: أن معنى ليعلم الله : ليرى , فعبر عن الرؤية بالعلم لأنها تؤول إليه , قاله الكلبي .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God will make His allies know who fears Him unseen.
rows.anchor: ليعلم أولياؤه من يخافه بالغيب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that people should know God knows who fears Him unseen.
rows.anchor: لتعلموا أن الله يعلم من يخافه بالغيب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth takes the phrase to command people to fear God unseen; “knowledge” is figurative, and unseen means privately as they fear Him publicly.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { بالغيب } يعني بالسر كما تخافونه في العلانية .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who transgresses after the prohibition is one who continues to hunt after the ban; painful punishment means painful.
rows.anchor: يعني فمن اعتدى في الصيد بعد ورود النهي .

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed at Hudaybiya, when game crowded around people in consecration.
rows.anchor: نزلت يوم الحديبية وقد غشي الصيد الناس وهم محرمون .

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: The majority take “while you are consecrated” to mean consecration for pilgrimage or minor pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: يعني الإحرام بحج أو عمرة , قاله الأكثرون .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes it to mean being inside the sanctuary; the verb can indicate entering a region, as in entering Tihama or Najd.
rows.anchor: يعني بالحرم الداخل إلى الحرم , يقال أحرم إذا دخل في الحرم , وأتهم إذا دخل تهامة , وأنجد إذا دخل نجد
